Synoptic Arctic Survey 2021 - metatranscriptomics

Author

geweaa

Published

November 20, 2024

The raw data was procesesd using nf-core/metatdenovo (v1.0.1): https://nf-co.re/metatdenovo/1.0.1/ The following command was used to start the pipeline: nextflow run nf-core/metatdenovo -r dev -profile uppmax -params-file params.yaml The file params.yaml contained the following relevant parameters: skip_kofamscan: TRUE orf_caller: ‘prokka’ eukulele_db: ‘gtdb-r220’ input: ‘input.csv’ project: naiss2024-22-406

Apart from this, the pipeline was run on default parameters. GTDB release 220 was used for taxonomic annotation.

For more information, see [1]

tpm <- read_tsv("data/megahit.prokka.counts.tsv.gz", show_col_types = F) %>% 
  select(orf, sample, count, tpm) %>%
  mutate(sample = gsub("R", ".", sample)) %>%
  mutate(sample = factor(sample, levels = c(
    "S1.1", "S1.2", "S2.1", "S2.2", "S3.1", "S3.2", "S4.1", "S4.2", "S5.1", "S6.1", 
    "S5.2", "S6.2", "S7.1", "S7.2", "S8.1", "S8.2", "S9.1", "S9.2", "S10.1", "S10.2"
  )))

meta <- read_tsv("data/sample_key.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  rename_with(tolower) %>%
  mutate(station = as.character(station)) %>%
  mutate(sample = gsub("R", ".", sample)) %>%
  select(-`user id`, -`>=q30(%)`) %>%
  mutate(sample = factor(sample, levels = c(
    "S1.1", "S1.2", "S2.1", "S2.2", "S3.1", "S3.2", "S4.1", "S4.2", "S5.1", "S6.1", 
    "S5.2", "S6.2", "S7.1", "S7.2", "S8.1", "S8.2", "S9.1", "S9.2", "S10.1", "S10.2"
  )))

In total, there are 20 metatranscriptomes from five stations. At every station, samples were taken in duplicates from 10 m depth and from chl. max. On average, each sample has 81.2 million reads (sd 8.7, n = 20). Off all the transcripts, 53.0 % was functionally annotated (Eggnog mapper), 36.5 % was functionally annotated including a KO reference, 45.7 % of the transcripts was annotated on phylum level, 45.7 % on order level, 44.8 % on genus level, and 32.7 % on species level.

25.2 % of the transcript were functionally annotated with Prokka. A summary of the bioinformatic pipeline will soon be added to this introduction.

Data exploration

Expand code 
tpm %>%
  inner_join(tax, by = "orf") %>%
  inner_join(meta, by = "sample") %>%
  group_by(sample, domain) %>% summarise(tpm = sum(tpm), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(domain %in% c("Bacteria", "Archaea")) %>%
  mutate(sample = factor(sample, levels = c(
    "S1.1", "S1.2", "S3.1", "S3.2", "S5.1", "S6.1", "S7.1", "S7.2", "S9.1", "S9.2", 
    "S2.1", "S2.2", "S4.1", "S4.2", "S5.2", "S6.2", "S8.1", "S8.2", "S10.1", "S10.2"
  ))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = sample,
    y = tpm,
    fill = domain
  )) +
  geom_col() + 
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 2e5, 4e5), labels = c(0, 2, 4)) +
  labs(y = expression('Relative abundance (tpm '%*% '10'^'5'*')')) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Bacteria" = "#C7B19C", "Archaea" = "#A2A475")) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_blank()
  ) +
  annotate("segment", x =  0.55, xend =  10.45, y = -25000, yend = -25000) +
  annotate("segment", x =  10.55, xend = 20.45, y = -25000, yend = -25000) +
  annotate("label", x = 5, y = -25000, label = "10 m", label.size = 0, size = 7/.pt) +
  annotate("label", x = 15, y = -25000, label = "Chl. max", label.size = 0, size = 7/.pt)

Community composition - phylum

Figure 1 explores the data by plotting the most abundant phyla over all samples, regardless if the RNA transcript was functionally annotated or not. Note that the taxonomy is outdated and needs to be updated (e.g. Pseudomonadota instead of Proteobacteria). 87.7 % of the annotated ORFs are affiliated with bacteria, while 13.1 % is affiliated with Archaea.

Expand code

  left_join(taxref, by = "orf") %>%
  replace_na(list("topphylum" = "Unidentified")) %>%

Beta diversity using NMDS (all stations)

As the metatranscriptomes from station 5 seem off (especially the duplicates), the ordination is run with (a) and without (b) this station. On a first glance it seems that the samples from 10 m depth and chlorophyll max. have been mixed up. The NMDS is run with default parameters.

Expand code 
set.seed(999)

nmds <- tpm %>%
  # Sum the abundance of both coverage per metagenome
  inner_join(eggnog, by = "orf") %>%
  # Filter out NA and add multiple KOs on new line
  filter(kegg_module != "-") %>% separate_rows(kegg_module, sep = ",") %>%
  # Sum the abundance of each KO within the metagenomes
  group_by(sample, kegg_module) %>% 
  summarise(tpm = sum(tpm), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Pivot to prepare a numerical matrix
  pivot_wider(names_from = "kegg_module", values_from = "tpm", values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample") %>%
  vegan::metaMDS()

nmds
Expand code 
nmds.scores <- vegan::scores(nmds)$sites %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("sample")
Expand code 
p1 <- nmds.scores %>%
  inner_join(meta, by = "sample") %>%
  mutate(station = factor(station, levels = names(cols.station))) %>%
  # Plot
  ggplot(aes(x = NMDS1, 
             y = NMDS2, 
             colour = station,
             shape = depth
             )) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 'dotted', linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 'dotted', linewidth = 0.25) +
  # Points for samples, coloured by site
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_shape_discrete(labels = c("10 m", "Chl. max"), name = "") +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols.station, name = "Station") +
  theme_tidy() +
  annotate('text', x = -Inf, y = -Inf, size = 7/.pt,
           label = paste('Stress = ', round(nmds$stress, digits = 2)),
           hjust = -0.1, vjust = -0.5) +
  theme(
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin()),
    panel.border = element_rect(linewidth = 0.75, colour = "black", fill = NA),
    legend.text = element_text(margin = margin(l = 0)),
    legend.box.margin = margin(l = -8)
    )

Beta diversity using NMDS

In this NMDS, the replicates from station 5 (S1 and S2) are removed prior to running the NMDS.

Expand code 
set.seed(555)

nmds <- tpm %>%
  filter(!sample %in% c("S1.1", "S1.2", "S2.1", "S2.2")) %>%
  # Sum the abundance of both coverage per metagenome
  inner_join(eggnog, by = "orf") %>%
  # Filter out NA and add multiple KOs on new line
  filter(kegg_module != "-") %>% separate_rows(kegg_module, sep = ",") %>%
  # Sum the abundance of each KO within the metagenomes
  group_by(sample, kegg_module) %>% 
  summarise(tpm = sum(tpm), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Pivot to prepare a numerical matrix
  pivot_wider(names_from = "kegg_module", values_from = "tpm", values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample") %>%
  vegan::metaMDS()

Expand code 
library(patchwork)

Figure 4 depicts the results on the NMDS for all stations (a) and for the NMDS with station 5 removed (b). The shape of the sample depicts the depth of the sample. Note that there is a considerable variations among the depth of chlorophyll max. For example, the chl. max. of station 56 is at 20 m, while chl. max of station 42 is at 45 m depth. Possibly this could be an explanation why the four samples of the two depths from station 56 are more similar?

  plot.tag.position = c(0.1, 1.05)
)

Differential gene expression using edgeR

Expand code 
library(edgeR)

m <- tpm %>%
  filter(!sample %in% c("S1.1","S1.2","S2.1","S2.2")) %>% # Leave out station 5 for the moment
  select(-tpm) %>%
  arrange(sample) %>%
  pivot_wider(values_from = "count", names_from = "sample", values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("orf") # Create a numeric matrix

dge <- tpm %>%
  filter(!sample %in% c("S1.1","S1.2","S2.1","S2.2")) %>% # Leave out station 5 for the moment
  select(-tpm) %>%
  inner_join(eggnog, by = "orf") %>% separate_longer_delim(kegg_ko, delim = ",") %>%
  group_by(sample, kegg_ko) %>% summarise(count = sum(count), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(kegg_ko != "-") %>%
  arrange(sample) %>%
  pivot_wider(values_from = "count", names_from = "sample", values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("kegg_ko") %>%
  DGEList(group = meta %>% filter(station != 5) %>% pull(depth), lib.size = colSums(m))
Expand code 
design.mat <- model.matrix(~ 0 + meta %>% filter(station != 5) %>% arrange(sample) %>% pull(depth))
rownames(design.mat) <- colnames(m)
colnames(design.mat) <- c("shallow", "deep")
contrast <- makeContrasts(depth = shallow-deep, levels = design.mat)

dge <- dge %>%
  calcNormFactors() %>%
  estimateDisp(design.mat) %>%
  glmQLFit(design.mat, robust = TRUE)

qlf <- glmQLFTest(dge, contrast = contrast)
Expand code 
de <- topTags(qlf, adjust.method = "fdr", n = Inf) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("kegg_ko") %>% rename_with(tolower) %>%
  mutate(expression = case_when(
    fdr < 0.05 & logfc > 0 ~ "up",
    fdr < 0.05 & logfc < 0 ~ "down",
    .default = "non-de"
  )) %>%
  inner_join(eggnog, by = "kegg_ko")

As the contrast was shallow vs deep, upregulated means significantly higher in the shallow samples while downregulated means higher in the deeper samples. There are 373 KOs up regulated and 763 KOs down regulated. 8025 KOs were not differential expressed.

  "Pelagibacter" = "#D69C4E",

  "ASP10-02a" = "#00A08A",
  "Sneathiella" = "#D8B70A",

  "Sneathiellaceae uncl." = "#046C9A",
  "Rhizobiales uncl. uncl." = "#D5D5D3"
)
  

top.de <- de %>%
  filter(expression != "non-de") %>%
  inner_join(tax, by = "orf") %>% inner_join(tpm, by = "orf") %>%
  filter(genus %in% t) %>%
  group_by(genus, kegg_ko, expression) %>% summarise(logfc = mean(logfc), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(expression) %>% slice_max(abs(logfc), n = 25) %>% ungroup()

The 25 KOs with the lowest (up in deeper samples) and 25 with the highest log fold-change are selected. Six of these KOs are represented in the gene list, the other 19 will be manually categorized. The number of 25 was arbitrary chosen. Many of these KOs are affiliated with the archaeon Nitrosopumilus that oxidizes ammonium and is capable of autotrophic growth using the hydroxypropionate/hydroxybutyrate cycle that is more energy efficient than other aerobic C fixation pathways, including the Calvin cycle (source: https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1402028111). The fact that C fixation KOs affiliated with this genus are abundantly detected strongly suggests autotrophic growth, possibly due to a low concentration of organic carbon.
